excerpt: ZenBusiness helps US entrepreneurs form an LLC or corporation and stay compliant, with plans from $0 plus state fees. Pricing, history and alternatives.
content:
ZenBusiness is an Austin, Texas company that helps people in the US start and run a small business. Its core service is business formation: it checks whether a name is available, prepares the Articles of Organization or Incorporation and files them with the state. Around that it sells compliance filings, registered agent service, an EIN application, domain and email, and other add-ons, and it offers a free AI guide called Velo that it says helps owners plan, file and stay on top of deadlines.

According to its About page, Ross Buhrdorf and Shanaz Hemmati co-founded ZenBusiness in 2015; Buhrdorf is its founder and CEO. The company says it has helped launch more than 950,000 businesses.

Funding

In November 2021 ZenBusiness announced a $200 million Series C at a $1.7 billion valuation, led by Oak HC/FT with SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and existing investors Cathay Innovation and Greycroft. The announcement also said investor Mark Cuban would join as an advocate and spokesperson.

Pricing

ZenBusiness publishes three formation plans. Starter costs $0 plus state fees and does not renew. Pro costs $199 plus state fees and renews at $199 a year, adding one-day processing, ongoing state compliance filings and an EIN. Premium costs $299 plus state fees and renews at $299 a year, adding a domain with privacy, a business email address and extra compliance protection. State filing fees are separate and vary by state.

Who it suits

It is aimed at first-time founders, freelancers and side businesses in the US that want filings handled for them. People forming a company outside the US, or founders who are comfortable filing directly with their Secretary of State, may not need it.

We have not used ZenBusiness. This page is based on its own website and pricing page (checked 15 October 2026) and its Series C announcement.
